study.question: Observation: g2-r0018-event_first exactly reproduced selected g2-r0017-aligned_centroid click AUC 0.6638436194 at the frozen seed after unused second-moment work was pruned (381.40s versus 387.97s, not an independent repeat). Moving normalization after raw slot averaging in g2-r0018-slot_first reduced click AUC to 0.6636177878 while reducing wall to361.18s and batch p50 to22.91ms from26.83ms. Its zero-similarity control g2-r0018-slot_null scored0.6635213077, so the small positive descriptor gap is preliminary. Does this normalization-order tradeoff arise from losing directional concentration, changing the event-norm weighting of directions, or both? Can a pooled mean-norm denominator preserve useful cancellation at lower measured cost than per-event cosine?
study.hypothesis: Let x_i be one field embedding for a valid event in a slot, l_i=max(norm(x_i),1e-8), and q=normalize(target,eps=1e-8). Equal-event vector e=mean(x_i/l_i) retains directional cancellation. Norm-weighted vector w=mean(x_i)/mean(l_i) is the mean of x_i/l_i weighted by l_i and is bounded by one. Existing raw-slot cosine uses normalize(mean(x_i)), removing resultant length and weighting direction by event norm. The falsifiable hypothesis is that retaining length in w recovers part of the click-quality loss of raw-slot cosine while using per-slot coordinate division rather than per-event coordinate division and similarity. A 2x2 replacement of angular population (equal versus norm_weighted) and concentration readout (retained versus unit) separates these effects conditional on all inherited raw-value paths. This is an unmeasured hypothesis about this offline benchmark, not a claim that concentration measures uncertainty or that all compressed information is recovered.

study.proposed_difference: Implement four standalone modules differing only in two literal architecture switches: norm_retained(candidate), equal_retained(equivalence control), equal_unit(control), norm_unit(raw-slot equivalence control). All compute masked per-event field norms and their scalar slot means. Equal cells divide event keys by pointwise norms before FP32 slot pooling; norm-weighted cells pool raw keys first. Retained equal uses the resulting vector directly; retained norm uses raw mean divided by the scalar norm mean; unit cells normalize the pre-denominator mean with inherited eps1e-8. Only then contract the30 slot vectors with aligned and coordinate-rotated unit target vectors, with squared aligned output as the third channel. No covariance, learned event projection, extra source, task identity, or new parameter. Unit cells need not equal retained/normalized vectors in the epsilon-active regime; preserve this numerical distinction explicitly. The norm_unit control performs scalar norm work absent in the historical slot_first, so their costs are not execution-equivalent.
predictions: For fixed weights outside numerical tolerances, equal_retained channels equal the masked mean per-event cosine and squared mean used by g2-r0018-event_first. Norm_unit channels equal g2-r0018-slot_first. Moving contraction is algebraic equivalence, not exact trained-trajectory equality.

Retained descriptors have field-vector norms at most1 (FP32 tolerance), vanish on empty slots, and equal their unit counterparts for collinear same-direction nonzero event fields outside epsilon. Mixed opposing directions reduce retained magnitude.

Primary predicted contrast: AUC(norm_retained)>AUC(norm_unit). Equal_retained versus equal_unit tests the same concentration hypothesis in the equal-event population. Evaluate both simple effects and their interaction; mixed signs mean population-specific evidence.

Secondary quality-cost prediction: norm_retained achieves click AUC within0.0002 of equal_retained, with at least5 percent lower measured train seconds or model-only p50. This is a provisional practical target, not an equivalence margin or significance test. Measure wall/GPU/memory/throughput too; no saving is assumed from algebra.

Use existing fixed history bins (empty,1..16,17..64,>64) with samples/positive/negative counts. Expect any concentration effect to be more plausible in multi-event slots; this is a diagnostic prediction, not a new confirmatory validation slice selected from outcomes.

Report four-task AUC/Logloss and auxiliary mean. Baseline DIN auxiliary AUCs0.8491/0.8649/0.8702 exceed selected ancestor0.7488/0.7748/0.7517, so a click gain cannot be described as universal multitask improvement.
falsifiers: Failure of either fixed-weight reference equivalence, output shapes, finite forward/backward, source-gradient ownership, masking/target-action isolation, initialization or Dice-state gates invalidates the implementation contrast; retain failure costs and do not reinterpret it as scientific counterevidence.

If both concentration-retaining simple effects are nonpositive, this implementation gives no support to the proposed retention mechanism. One negative branch does not refute all concentration-aware compression.
If only one angular population benefits, reject a population-independent explanation and inspect norm weighting/gradient interactions before generalizing.

If norm_retained misses the quality-cost target, do not claim an efficient approximation. If scalar norms add more time/memory than avoided work saves, the cost hypothesis fails even when click AUC improves.

If equal_retained materially departs from the event-first reference after training (predeclared diagnostic flag absolute click-AUC delta>0.0001), investigate reduction/gradient sensitivity before using old and new endpoints as interchangeable controls. Same-weight tensor agreement alone does not prove trajectory equivalence.
Small single-seed gaps, empty-history changes caused by training shared parameters, or favorable auxiliary means cannot establish the compression mechanism or replace the click selection score.

Norm weighting and equal weighting define different angular populations; their concentration lengths are not numerically the same statistic. Raw item means remain visible to the model in every cell.
